name: threadgroup-scratch-of-eighty-byte-elements
rationale: A [[threadgroup]] buffer whose element is an 80-byte AIR struct, bound by the caller at 2560 bytes -- 32 elements, one per lane. The element count was computed against a type-definition map collected before the pass synthesized the element type, and spirv_size_align answers one word for an id it cannot look up, so this element measured 4 bytes: the 2560-byte binding named 640 elements and the module declared 51200 bytes of threadgroup memory. Metal refuses any pipeline declaring more than 32768, so before the fix this case could not run at all. Nothing in the struct is one word on purpose -- uint4 v[5] is 80 bytes with no padding to argue about. Each lane writes its own element's first and last uint4 and then, after a threadgroup barrier, reads two OTHER lanes' elements, so the stride between elements is what the observation measures: out[lid] = 16a + 11b + 10 for a = (lid+1)&31 and b = (lid+2)&31, and a wrong element size puts the neighbours somewhere other than where their writer put them. Every slot read is written before the barrier, so no lane observes Metal's undefined initial threadgroup contents and the answer does not depend on the executor's zero-fill.

name: division-flags-and-fast-sincos-without-fast-math
rationale: DESIGN D279 (WP-FMX2, refining D253.2 and D253.12): division-flags-and-fast-sincos-under-fast-math without fast math, where the plain operator carries no flag. Each of 512 threads writes 10 words: x / y and 1 / y (no flag), fast::divide(x, y) and (1, y) (reassoc nsz arcp contract afn), fast::divide of x and z by one load of y, fast::sincos(t)'s sine and cosine, and fast::sin(t) and fast::cos(t) (the fast intrinsics without flags). Words 10-15 keep the 0xAB poison. Operands (x, y): 160 generic quotients with exponents in [-20, 20]; 48 divisors about 2^126 (2^126 itself, its neighbours, 2^127, the largest float, values just below) with numerators whose correctly rounded quotient is a normal number; 48 quotients in or near the float denormals; 32 denormal divisors; 32 divisors about 2^-126; 32 pairs of zeros, infinities, NaN, and finite values; 32 quotients past or near the largest float; 32 powers of two and equal operands; the rest over the whole exponent range. z is a generic numerator. The angles t: 160 in [-2^-8, 4), 64 up to 2^22, 64 within 16 half-ulps of float(pi/2) * 2^22 = 6588397.5 of either sign, 96 past it up to the largest float, 16 special values (signed zeros, infinities, NaN, denormals, 2^-126, the largest float, the limit and its neighbour), and the rest in [-2^24, 2^24]. The AIR has no loop.

name: write-a-runtime-slot-through-a-dynamic-cursor-that-crosses-a-helper-call
rationale:
A DYNAMIC byte cursor into a RAW device buffer, crossing a helper call -- the half of the rule that had no representation at all until `b321137c`, and the companion of `write-slot-two-through-a-constant-cursor-that-crosses-a-helper-call`.

The emitter models a buffer raw when the shader also views it as bytes, and then a non-zero GEP of it has no SPIR-V pointer value: it is a `Private` zero placeholder, with the real descriptor root and byte offset held only in the emitter's `raw_offsets`. `raw_device_call_arg_id` can carry a CONSTANT cursor onto the callee's parameter -- one offset per (callee, parameter) is all it can record -- but a runtime offset has nowhere to live, and Logical addressing forbids handing the callee the derived pointer instead. `d974b76b` had to start refusing this shape because the fallback handed the callee the placeholder and every access it made landed in scratch. The only representation that keeps those accesses on the buffer is the one with no call boundary, so the translator now splices the refused call into its caller in the AIR text and emits that; the emitted module shows the helper's store arriving as `OpInBoundsAccessChain %_ptr_StorageBuffer_uint %buffer %uint_0 <runtime index>`.

`__attribute__((noinline))` is what keeps the helper in the AIR -- without it the frontend inlines it and there is no boundary to splice. The `uchar` view of the same buffer is what puts it on the raw model; a `float4`-only shader takes the typed access-chain path and never reaches this rule. `slot` is LOADED from the buffer, so the cursor is a runtime value the frontend cannot fold, and one thread is enough -- a `tid`-indexed cursor would fold to zero at `tid == 0` and prove nothing.

The answer discriminates the cursor exactly. The helper writes slot `slot` == 2 and the entry writes slot 0, so a cursor lost to scratch leaves slot 2 holding its -1.0 sentinel, and a cursor that collapsed to the buffer root would put the helper's vector in slot 0 before the entry overwrote it -- either way slot 2 is the discriminator. Slots 1 and 3 are written by nothing and hold -1.0, so an off-by-one cursor in either direction is visible too, and -1.0 is a value no arm can produce. `slot` and `seed` are read as BYTES -- byte 0 and byte 4 of the buffer -- so they are 2 and 5 exactly and no float rounding enters the answer; every written value is a small integer exactly representable in binary32. One thread, so nothing races.

Metal answered (5, 2, 0, 0), (-1, -1, -1, -1), (5, 6, 7, 8), (-1, -1, -1, -1), all sixteen floats derived in advance, and MoltenVK Matches.

name: precise-trigonometric-functions-at-nan-operands-under-fast-math
rationale: Thread i reads one float pattern x from in[i] and writes 12 words: precise::sin(x), precise::cos(x), the sine and cosine of precise::sincos(x), precise::tan(x), precise::asin(x), precise::acos(x), precise::atan(x), precise::asinh(x), precise::atanh(x), precise::atan2(x, 1) and x. Compiled with the default fast math, so each call carries every fast-math flag. x runs over 20 NaN patterns (quiet and signalling payloads of both signs), both zeros, both infinities, denormals and ordinary values of both signs inside and outside the domains of asin, acos and atanh. It measures which NaN Metal answers for these precise functions in their flagged state, which the NaN model does not carry across from their unflagged answers (docs/TODO.md 2.11).

name: erode-a-strip-whose-left-edge-wraps-onto-its-right
rationale:
A 7x7 erode over a 16x1 half4 strip whose only integer work is air.clamp.u.v2i16 -- and the clamp is UNSIGNED while the tap offset it clamps is a signed -3..3 added to the coordinate. At gx=0 the offsets -3,-2,-1 become 0xFFFD..0xFFFF as u16, so they clamp to the RIGHT edge (x=15) instead of to zero, and the left three columns of the output sample pixel 15. That is what the payload is built to expose: channel G is 100 everywhere except 4 at x=15 and 25 at x=8, so the first three outputs read 2 only if the wrap happened -- a signed clamp would leave them at 10. Channel A carries an independent pattern (81, with 9 at x=3 and 49 at x=15) so the two half lanes cannot cover for each other.
Exactness: R and B are zero, so texel.y - texel.x*texel.x is the stored channel with no rounding, every stored value is far above the 0xH068E floor so air.fmax never fires, and every value is a perfect square (4, 9, 25, 49, 81, 100) whose half square root is the exact integer 2, 3, 5, 7, 9 or 10. Because sqrt is monotonic the min-of-sqrt equals the sqrt-of-min, so the answer is an integer regardless of the order the 49 taps are folded in.

name: srgb-encode-across-the-threshold-with-an-exact-one
rationale: One invocation with pixel_index 0, so the stride multiplies to zero and the three linear channels are read at element 0. air.fast_powr.v3f32 is an approximation with no accuracy guarantee, and this sRGB encode raises each channel to the float nearest -7/12, so the only argument at which the answer is representable independently of the implementation is one: powr(1, y) is exactly 1 for every y. Channel 1 is authored 1.0 and takes the gamma arm, where 1.055f * 1 - 0.055f rounds to 0.99999994f -- the product is exact, so the fused and unfused forms of that multiply-add agree and the fast-math contract on the entry cannot move it. Channels 0 and 2 are 1/1024 and 1/4096, both under the 0.0031308 threshold, so they take the linear arm and are one correctly-rounded multiply by 12.92f each. The three results are distinct and not a palindrome, so the arm select, the threshold comparison, both scale constants, and the lane order all move the bytes if they are wrong. What this case does not separate is powr from a lowering that drops the call entirely, because the authored argument is its own answer; that is the price of the only exact point this exponent has.

name: a-record-whose-size-is-not-a-multiple-of-four
rationale:
The device proof for the third instance of the four-byte alignment floor. `struct Rec { short a[5]; uchar b[7]; }` has 17 bytes of members and an alignment of 2, so Metal's sizeof is 18 -- and Metal says so twice, in `air.arg_type_size, i32 18` on the buffer and in `sizes[tid]`, which the shader computes as `sizeof * 1000 + alignof` and which comes back 18002.

`spirv_size_align`'s struct arm in `src/layout.rs` started its running maximum at 4 rather than 1, so the record's alignment was reported as 4, its size as `round_up(17, 4) = 20`, and the buffer's `OpDecorate ArrayStride 20`. Every element but the zeroth was then addressed two bytes per record too far along. The same floor had already been removed from `raw_size_align` (`9993cca8`) and `memcpy_size_align` (`1c2d724d`); this was the third copy of one rule, and the one that reaches the emitted addresses. A fourth copy is still standing in `air_metadata_vulkan_block_size_align` (`src/native/ir/raw_buffer.rs`); removing it alone leaves this case's stride at 20, so it is a different consumer of the same rule and is not what this fixes.

The two stores are placed to catch the drift immediately and at two different member alignments: `a[3]` is a short at byte 6 of the record and `b[1]` a uchar at byte 11, so a wrong stride moves both, and the rest of the 576-byte buffer must still hold its fill. Thread 0 writes at the same place under either stride, so the case is deliberately 32 threads: the drift is 2 bytes at thread 1 and 62 bytes at thread 31.

The `.ll` is the Metal front end's own output for the sibling `.metal`, round-tripped through llvm-as/llvm-dis for opaque pointers -- not hand-written -- so nothing about the record's layout is my assertion. MEASURED: MoltenVK Mismatch before the fix and Match after, on the same case, with only `src/layout.rs` changed between the two runs.

name: saturating-halving-and-wide-product-integers-at-their-edges
rationale: The nine integer intrinsic arms this translator refused until now, each beside the sibling it mirrors, over a 12-value edge grid rotated so every value meets every other. addsat and subsat at INT_MIN and INT_MAX, where the clamp end is the sign of the first operand and not of the wrapped result; hadd and rhadd at -1, where the signed form must round toward -inf and the unsigned form must not sign-extend; mulhi, madhi and madsat at products that overflow 32 bits, where madhi wraps its addend into the high half while madsat clamps the 64-bit sum, so the two disagree. Rows 10 through 14 repeat the halving and saturating families at 16 bits, 8 bits and three 8-bit lanes, which carry no widening at all, so the width and the lane count are the whole risk. Every operand is read from a buffer so nothing folds to a constant.

name: loads-and-stores-past-a-loaded-pointers-buffer
rationale: Eight threads (DESIGN D245, the loaded pointer form): the argument buffer h (binding 1) holds at byte 0 the address of p, a separately owned 16-byte buffer (words 0xD1000001 to 0xD1000004), so the kernel reaches p through a pointer it loads from memory (a dynamic root, D76). idx = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 17, 63, then 4, 6, 9, 12, 30, 44, 50, 63. Thread t loads p[idx[t]] into out[t] (threads 4 to 7 load past p's 16 bytes, within its 256-byte reach, results Metal leaves undefined) and stores 0xB0000000 | t to p[idx[8 + t]], every store past p's end (words 4 to 63, within its reach). The output is out: p's four words, then the four reads (bytes 16 to 31, the declared out-of-bounds reads of p).

name: ten-shuffles-across-one-simdgroup
rationale: Metal ground truth for ten uncovered shuffle families: air.simd_shuffle_xor.v4f16 (2 case-less corpus sources), air.simd_shuffle_xor.v2f16 (2), air.simd_shuffle_up.v3f16 (2), air.simd_shuffle_down.u.v4i16 (2), air.simd_shuffle_and_fill_down.v2f16 (2), air.simd_prefix_exclusive_sum.v4f32 (2), air.simd_xor.u.v2i16 (2), air.quad_shuffle_xor.f16 (2), air.quad_shuffle_xor.v2f16 (2) and air.quad_shuffle_xor.v3f16 (2) -- 20 sources. One 32-thread threadgroup is one SIMD group here, so every lane is known. A shuffle is only evidence if the lane it reads is not the lane it runs on, so every source value is a function of tid and every read lands elsewhere -- an xor by 1, 2 or 3, a step up by one lane, a step down by one -- and the components of each vector are scaled apart, so a lowering that shuffled component 0 and broadcast it, or that swizzled, lands a value the derivation places on another component. simd_shuffle_up at lane 0 and simd_shuffle_down at lane 31 read a lane that does not exist and Metal leaves that undefined, so those two lanes store a sentinel rather than record undefined behaviour; the shuffles still run on every lane, because a shuffle is convergent and a lowering that sank one into the guarded branch is a bug this fixture must not hide. simd_shuffle_and_fill_down needs no guard -- lane 31 steps off the end into the filling vector, which is what the family is for. The exclusive prefix sum is stored with one added: at lane 0 an exclusive scan is the identity, and Metal returns -0.0 for the float one where MoltenVK returns +0.0, which is the signed-zero divergence measured across this family and not something a case can assert; adding one lands both on exactly 1.0 and leaves every other lane at i * (i - 1) + 1, still exact and still different from the inclusive scan. Every other value is an integer below 128 or an exact binary fraction.
